item.title: Understanding behavior in real-world contexts
item.content:encoded:
Dolores Albarracin, University of Pennsylvania

Mandy Hütter, University of Zurich

Zachary A. Niese, Montclair State University

This special section seeks research that bridges laboratory-based psychological science with real-world contexts and consequential behavior. While researchers have identified many important psychological processes, much existing work isolates these processes from the social and ecological environments where they actually operate. The special section aims to advance understanding of how psychological processes function within the environments people inhabit and their relationship to behavior that matters beyond the research setting.

Appel publié par Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Environmental properties and psychological processes
  • Informational, institutional, and cultural environments
  • Physical environments and behavior
  • Psychological processes and real-world behavior
  • Person-environment transactions
  • Beliefs and attitudes in context
  • Memory and consequential outcomes

  • Oliver Sng, National University of Singapore
